description: SELECT * over a USING or NATURAL join projects the join key ONCE, and FIRST - all live-verified on a real account. t1(a,k,b) JOIN t2(c,k,d) USING (k) projects K A B C D, so the merged key moves to the FRONT rather than staying in the left table's position; USING (y, x) surfaces the keys in USING-LIST order while a NATURAL join uses LEFT-TABLE order; a chained JOIN t3 USING (j) puts J before the earlier K; the keys stay in front through a later ON join; and the same key joined twice still projects once. On an OUTER join the merged column is the first NON-NULL of the two sides' copies, and a BARE reference to the key name resolves to that merged value in every context - SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY - while a QUALIFIED reference still reads its OWN side, nulls included. Qualified stars keep each side's full layout with nothing merged, EXCLUDE applies to the merged column, the merged shape survives beside a WINDOW function (whose projection reshapes rows itself) and it flows into CTAS as four declared columns rather than five. Frostlake used to return the combined row UN-projected - four declared columns but five values per row - so every consumer reading by index silently shifted one slot, which is why the Java asserted the row WIDTH against the column list on every row. Converted 1:1 from query/UsingJoinProjectionTest (now retired); expect.columns and the row sets together carry that width check.
